catalog_quote: Maurer 2013 (APiCS ch. 36, Phonology): "The tonal system of Angolar is not fully investigated, yet a preliminary analysis of disyllabic nouns in subject position followed by a disyllabic verb modified by the future marker ka shows that there exist four different tone melodies (HH, HL, LH, LL), which points to a two-tone system (own fieldwork, 2008): (1) áwá ká gàʃtà 'The water will be wasted.' ... fóθà ká kàbà 'The energy will come to an end.' ... kàθó ká pèndè 'The dog will get lost.' ... The syllable structure is of the (C)V type; up to four syllables are possible: a-dha 'wing', ne-ne-ka 'to endanger', or ma-ra-ka-tho 'demarcation'." Bandeira, Agostinho & Freitas 2021, fn. 4: "Em relação ao angolar, Maurer (1995) e Lorenzino (1998) propõem que o angolar apresenta tom lexical, mas não apresentam uma análise fonológica aprofundada. Neste trabalho, não abordaremos a descrição do sistema …

tone_statements.citation: Bandeira, Manuele, Ana Lívia Agostinho & Shirley Freitas. 2021. Aspectos fonético-fonológicos do angolar moderno. Alfa: Revista de Linguística (São José do Rio Preto) 65: e13177, 31 pp. doi:10.1590/1981-5794-e13177
tone_statements.quote: Em relação ao angolar, Maurer (1995) e Lorenzino (1998) propõem que o angolar apresenta tom lexical, mas não apresentam uma análise fonológica aprofundada. Neste trabalho, não abordaremos a descrição do sistema suprassegmental do angolar, que será foco de pesquisas futuras, e utilizaremos a marcação acento para indicar a proeminência lexical. [...] O acento primário foi indicado – somente nas transcrições fonéticas – pelo símbolo (ˈ) antecedendo a sílaba tônica como em [ˈbudʊ] ‘pedra’ em angolar. [...] Embora a lista de 1600 itens de Maurer (1995) reúna o léxico básico do angolar e, em alguns casos, informação tonal, os dados apresentam uma notação gráfica sem transcrição fonética ou notação fonológica, sobretudo, sem qualquer referência à posição do acento primário.
tone_statements.translation: As for Angolar, Maurer (1995) and Lorenzino (1998) propose that Angolar has lexical tone, but do not present an in-depth phonological analysis. In this work we will not address the description of the suprasegmental system of Angolar, which will be the focus of future research, and we will use stress marking to indicate lexical prominence. [...] Primary stress was indicated - only in the phonetic transcriptions - by the symbol (ˈ) preceding the stressed syllable, as in [ˈbudʊ] 'stone' in Angolar. [...] Although Maurer's (1995) 1600-item list gathers the basic lexicon of Angolar and, in some cases, tonal information, the data are given in a graphic notation without phonetic transcription or phonological notation and, above all, without any reference to the position of primary stress.
tone_statements.locator: note 4 (end notes, on the suprasegmental system); 'Materiais e métodos' paragraph on Maurer's 1600-item list; notation paragraph following note 4 (stress mark); section on long vowels (two tones per bimoraic syllable, after Agostinho 2015)
tone_statements.summary: No analysis of its own: lexical tone claimed by Maurer 1995/Lorenzino 1998 is reported as unverified; authors transcribe word stress and defer the suprasegmental system to future research.

tone_statements.citation: Yakpo, Kofi. 2021. Creole prosodic systems are areal, not simple. Frontiers in Psychology 12: 690593. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2021.690593
tone_statements.quote: Tone systems are also found in the insular Gulf of Guinea Portuguese-lexifier Creoles Forro (Maurer, 2008) and Angolar (Maurer, 1995), spoken in São Tomé, Lung’le (Agostinho and Hyman, 2021), spoken in Príncipe, and Fa d’Ambô, spoken in Annobón. Fa d’Ambô and Lung’Ie have been analyzed as languages with a privative /H, Ø/ contrast, based on the stress contrast of Portuguese.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: both deciding quotations are verbatim in the copies we hold at the stated places. The classification tonal rests on a 2013 APiCS grammar sketch by the principal fieldworker (own 2008 data), and the APiCS Tone datapoint 36-120 downloaded now independently codes Angolar 'Simple tone system, for lexical and grammatical distinctions' with Confidence: Certain, so the record faithfully reports the only committed analysis in the literature. It is not 'well-sourced' because (a) Maurer himself calls the analysis preliminary and says his 1995 treatment 'has to be seriously amended'; (b) neither full grammar (Maurer 1995, Lorenzino 1998) is. (c) a competing reading exists: Bandeira 2017 (pp. 259–260, 313; held by the project under saot1239, read now) treats Angolar as having primary stress on the final, penultimate or antepenultimate syllable and remarks that Maurer's tone examples look like tone 'confundid
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again: re-done independently. (1) Maurer 2013 APiCS survey ch. 36 'Phonology' — the deciding quotation is verbatim in lines 133-151 ('The tonal system of Angolar is not fully investigated, yet a preliminary analysis of disyllabic nouns.. four different tone melodies (HH, HL, LH, LL), which points to a two-tone system (own fieldwork, 2008)'; examples áwá ká gàʃtà / fóθà ká kàbà / kàθó ká pèndè / àlè ká pɛ̀nθà; 'Tonal distinctions are also used in order to differentiate syntactic categories.. ðùrà 'to help' vs. ðúrá 'help''; the (C)V / ma-ra-ka-tho syllable sentence at line 2

sources.quote: p. 259–260: 'Quanto ao angolar, pouco se sabe sobre o suposto sistema tonal defendido por Maurer (1995) ... Para o angolar, Maurer (1995: 9) propõe dois tons: H e L ... HH (mámá ["mama] ‘seio’), LL (màmà [ma"ma] ‘amamentar’), HL (mótxì ["mOti] ‘morte’) e LH (bòbó [bO"bO] ‘maduro’) ... sources.note: First-hand segmental phonology (16 consonants, 7 short + 7 long oral vowels, syllable templates) of modern Angolar; explicitly reports that Maurer 1995 and Lorenzino 1998 claim lexical tone without a full analysis, declines to analyse the suprasegmental system (future work) and transcribes a primary-stress mark per word instead; for long vowels it adopts Agostinho's (2015) Lung'Ie structure in which a two-tone sequence is assigned to the bimoraic syllable, one tone per mora. Documents the unresolved tone-vs-stress status from the fieldworkers' side.
